result.summary: Fixes scanblocks so that a failed LookupFilterRange call is reported to the caller instead of being silently skipped. Mirrors getblockfilter's error classification: throws a 'still indexing' error when the block filter index is behind the tip and the requested range is not yet available, and an internal error if lookup fails after the index is synced. Adds a functional test that reproduces the unindexed-range scenario by wiping and rebuilding the filter index.
result.problem: scanblocks previously advanced past any unindexed chunk while still returning completed:true, hiding a gap where matches in that range were never checked. This silently gives callers, such as wallets rescanning via block filters, an incomplete relevant_blocks list they cannot distinguish from a clean 'no matches' result.

resolved_concerns: fjahr pointed out the initial fix incorrectly failed unconditionally whenever the index was behind the tip, unlike getblockfilter which only fails if the specific range is unavailable; author reworked the PR (two force pushes) to mirror getblockfilter's actual behavior and confirmed the fix.

result.card: This PR fixes bitcoind's scanblocks RPC so that a failed block-filter range lookup is reported as an error instead of being silently skipped while the call still returns completed:true, which previously let callers receive an incomplete relevant_blocks list indistinguishable from a genuinely empty scan. The fix mirrors getblockfilter's existing error classification: 'still being indexed' while the filter index lags the tip and hasn't yet covered the requested range, or an internal error if lookup fails once the index is synced. A maintainer (fjahr) initially flagged the first version as failing unconditionally whenever the index was behind the tip, unlike getblockfilter; the author reworked the PR to match getblockfilter's actual per-range logic, and maflcko gave a Concept ACK on the underlying regression. The PR is a first-time contributor's fix, found via AI-assisted review but independently confirmed as a real correctness gap by a maintainer. No open concerns remain and no dependencies are noted; it is ready for a follow-up code review of the reworked patch.
